## An experiment in 2010

Does DNA really control a cell? In 2010, J. Craig Venter and his team studied the complete DNA sequence of a simple bacterium, *Mycoplasma mycoides*, using a computer.

<!-- STEP -->
## Copy, then swap

They chemically made an exact copy of this DNA in the laboratory. Then they took a closely related bacterium and removed its DNA. They kept the rest of the cell, such as its cytoplasm and cell membrane.

<!-- STEP -->
## The cell follows the new DNA

They inserted the synthetic DNA into this cell. The cell grew and divided, following the instructions from the new DNA.

**So DNA controls the structure and activities of a cell.**

<!-- STEP -->
## What they did not do

The team did not create a new cell from scratch. Only the DNA was synthetic. The other parts came from a living cell. A living cell, too, comes only from another cell, and the next lesson shows how one cell becomes two.
